lesson.title: Excel VLOOKUP Basics
lesson.description: Learn how VLOOKUP finds a value in the first column of a table and returns a matching value from another column. You will read each argument, choose exact match, and fix the most common errors.

content.title: Lookup value
content.content: The value VLOOKUP searches for in the first column of the table, such as a product ID.
content.example: In =VLOOKUP(A2, D2:F20, 3, FALSE), A2 is the lookup value.

content.title: Column index number
content.content: The position of the column to return, counted from the left edge of the table range, starting at 1.
content.example: In the range D2:F20, column F is column index 3.

content.title: How VLOOKUP searches
content.content: VLOOKUP looks down the first (leftmost) column of the table range until it finds the lookup value, then moves right to the column given by the column index number and returns that cell. It can only look to the right of the first column.
key_points: It always searches the leftmost column of the range
The column index counts from that leftmost column
It returns the first match it finds

content.title: Exact match with FALSE
content.content: The last argument controls matching. FALSE (or 0) asks for an exact match and returns #N/A when the value is missing. TRUE or leaving it out asks for an approximate match, which only works when the first column is sorted in ascending order.
key_points: Use FALSE for IDs, names and codes
#N/A usually means the value was not found

content.question: In =VLOOKUP(A2, D2:F20, 3, FALSE), which column's value is returned?
content.explanation: The column index 3 counts from the first column of the range D2:F20: D is 1, E is 2, F is 3.

content.question: Your VLOOKUP returns #N/A for a product ID you can see in the table. What is the most likely cause?
options: The column index number is too small
The ID has an extra space or is stored as text
The table range is too large
content.correct_answer: The ID has an extra space or is stored as text
content.explanation: With exact match, the lookup value must match exactly. A trailing space or a number stored as text makes them different, so VLOOKUP reports #N/A.

content.question: Why can't VLOOKUP return a value from a column to the left of the lookup column?
options: It only searches the leftmost column and returns columns to its right
Excel blocks formulas that look left
The column index number cannot be 1
It needs the data sorted first
content.correct_answer: It only searches the leftmost column and returns columns to its right
content.explanation: VLOOKUP searches the first column of the range, and the column index counts to the right from there, so columns to the left cannot be reached.
